A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RecAD and the same empirical work despite retitling and substantial reorganization. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout, including v2 Appendices A–B; v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 Section 5 reports original recourse and anomaly-detection experiments on Linear, Lotka-Volterra and MSDS, including ablations, sensitivity analysis and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix B.3. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original results produced by the work.

M1.justification: The GVAR model, LSTM/FFNN action predictor and additive counterfactual propagation remain. V2 Eq. (7) drops the threshold multiplier and explicit cost weighting from v1 Eq. (12), although Appendix B.2 retains the cost-vector discussion. Algorithm 1 also changes the stated update schedule from updates at individual abnormal steps during a series traversal to an update after an L-step rollout. These are limited reported procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Linear, Lotka-Volterra and MSDS, retaining synthetic point anomalies, externally caused sequence anomalies and structurally caused sequence anomalies. V2's external/structural terminology matches v1's non-causal/causal categories; it does not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: MLP, LSTM, VAR and GVAR remain the evaluated comparators in every corresponding synthetic and MSDS recourse comparison. The component-removal comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, anomaly proportions, recourse splits, window sizes 5/5/10, lookahead L=1 and network sizes are retained. Both use USAD and generate MSDS counterfactuals through GVAR/AAP. The action-cost formula loses explicit weighting, but both versions specify unit cost weights for the experiments, making the reported metric equivalent.

E4.justification: The same FFNN/LSTM ablations, lambda sensitivity analysis and Lotka-Volterra/MSDS case studies remain. Their questions and evidence are unchanged; reordering and renumbering do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report results with standard deviations over 10 runs. V2 consolidates this statement and explicitly calls the central values means, without establishing additional runs, new uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All matched numerical result entries are identical: v1 Tables 2–6 correspond to v2 Tables 6, 2, 3, 4 and 5. For example, MSDS RecAD retains a flipping ratio of 0.841±0.080 and action cost of 6.747±1.543. The sensitivity plots and case-study interventions are also unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 Sections 4.1 and 4.4 introduce constrained maximum-likelihood and penalized formulations, a cross-world posterior derivation, and an exponential distance-based backtracking conditional used to derive the action regularizer. This substantially expands the formal reasoning beyond v1's direct cost-regularized objective and AAP equations, even though the resulting loss has a similar structure.

C1.justification: V2 makes backtracking counterfactual explanations and constrained maximum-likelihood learning central contributions in its abstract, introduction and conclusion. V1 centers minimum-cost anomaly reversal with downstream effects. V2 also centers the formal formulation on external interventions, treating structural anomalies as an extension while retaining the empirical effectiveness claim.

C2.justification: V2 develops a new interpretation of recourse as plausible changes to exogenous variables while causal laws remain fixed. Section 4.5 additionally discusses unknown anomaly-sequence length and shortest corrective sequences, and explicitly leaves the significance of explaining structural interventions to future study. These materially revise the explanatory scope and qualifications of v1's treatment.

D1.justification: V2 adds hardware and software specifications in Appendix B.2 and changes the published code pointer from RecAD2023 to RecAD2025. However, it removes v1's detailed point/sequence anomaly-injection recipes, including trend, shapelet, seasonal and structural-change constructions, despite promising them in Appendix B. USAD training/scoring details and the dedicated streaming-inference description are also omitted. These are substantial documentation changes, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly positions RecAD relative to backtracking counterfactuals by von Kügelgen et al. (2023) and deep backtracking explanations by Kladny et al. (2024). It expands discussion of static-data recourse and explainable anomaly detection while removing several general anomaly-detection references. The relationship to prior research changes substantially.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related-work and preliminary subsections are reorganized; case studies precede ablation and sensitivity sections; algorithm, dataset and implementation material moves into new appendices. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added formal content.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column design, enlarges and redistributes displays, and restructures the external-anomaly results table from dataset column groups into dataset row blocks. Figure 2 is replaced by a backtracking diagram and timeline. Other empirical plots retain their content, while the detector-results table moves to Appendix B.3.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a more explicit formal rationale, clearer research positioning and more readable displays. However, it removes the anomaly-injection instructions needed to reconstruct its central synthetic evaluations, despite directing readers to Appendix B for them. With the empirical evidence unchanged, the gains in explanation and presentation cannot confidently be judged to outweigh this substantive reproducibility loss.
